clinical_category: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis - fibrotic restrictive physiology and impaired gas exchange
blueprint_topic: Pathophysiologic adaptation to progressive interstitial lung fibrosis
stem: A client with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis has progressive exertional dyspnea and a persistent dry cough. Which physiologic change best explains the progressive respiratory impairment?

options.A: Fibrotic scarring disrupts lung architecture, producing restrictive impairment with reduced compliance and impaired gas exchange
options.B: Loss of elastic recoil increases lung compliance in the same pattern as emphysema
options.C: The disorder is primarily a reversible bronchial smooth-muscle problem with normal interstitial architecture
options.D: Progressive fibrosis increases diffusing capacity and improves oxygen transfer across the alveolar-capillary interface

rationale: A is correct. Current NCBI/StatPearls sources describe idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis as a progressive scarring disorder in which dysregulated repair and matrix deposition destroy lung architecture and impair gas exchange. Restrictive lung disease caused by interstitial fibrosis is characterized by reduced lung volumes and impaired compliance, which increases the work of breathing and contributes to progressive dyspnea. B describes the increased-compliance physiology of emphysema rather than fibrosis. C incorrectly reduces the disorder to reversible bronchospasm. D is opposite to the expected effect because fibrotic interstitial disease is associated with reduced diffusing capacity and impaired oxygen transfer.
educational_objective: Relate progressive dyspnea in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis to interstitial scarring that reduces lung compliance, produces restrictive physiology, and impairs gas exchange.
source_document_title: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis; Restrictive Lung Disease
source_version_date: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis last updated 2024-04-23; Restrictive Lung Disease last updated 2025-11-08; current NCBI Bookshelf editions accessed 2026-08-18
source_locator: NCBI Bookshelf 'Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis' → Continuing Education Activity/Introduction: progressive scarring, progressive dyspnea and dry nonproductive cough; dysregulated repair causes matrix deposition/scarring, destroys lung architecture and impairs gas exchange; PFTs show restrictive impairment and diminished diffusing capacity. NCBI Bookshelf 'Restrictive Lung Disease' → Continuing Education Activity: restrictive disorders have reduced lung volumes and impaired compliance with compromised gas exchange; intrinsic interstitial diseases involve fibrotic processes in lung parenchyma.
source_claim_supported: Current NCBI/StatPearls content directly supports progressive fibrotic scarring with architectural destruction, restrictive physiology, decreased compliance/diffusing capacity, and impaired gas exchange as the mechanism underlying progressive respiratory symptoms in IPF.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

correction_summary: Substantive rebuild. The source used a generic ATS homepage and broad 'pulmonary fibrosis' language. The final item narrows the construct to idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and anchors the symptom and physiology claims to current NCBI/StatPearls sources with exact sections. The wording distinguishes reduced compliance in fibrosis from increased compliance in emphysema and avoids unsupported prognosis or treatment claims.
audit_findings: The original ATS root URL failed the exact-locator requirement.
Current NCBI/StatPearls IPF content directly supports progressive dry cough/dyspnea, fibrotic scarring, architectural destruction, restrictive impairment, and reduced diffusing capacity.
A newer 2025 StatPearls restrictive-lung-disease source directly verifies reduced compliance and compromised gas exchange in intrinsic fibrotic lung disease.
The final distractors contrast fibrosis with emphysema, reversible bronchospasm, and falsely improved diffusion without creating a second defensible answer.
Independent adversarial second pass found one uniquely correct answer, no unsupported quantitative PFT cutoff, no cueing, and no unresolved conflict.
